where: Section 2, also the second Exam trap and the Quiz Q5 answer
problem: The recommended procedure is backwards. It says to start at a low flash rate and stop at the first single still image. With one painted mark, a single still image also appears whenever the shaft makes a whole number of turns between flashes, that is at f = (n/60)/m for m = 2, 3, ... Sweeping up from below, the first single still image therefore appears at half (or a third) of the true speed, and the dial under-reads. The standard rule is to come down from a high rate, because the first single still image met from above is the true speed.
fix: Set the flash rate high (well above the expected rate) and lower it. The first single still image you reach is the true speed, f = p n / 60. Equivalently, take the highest flash rate that gives one still image. Do not sweep upward from a low rate.

problem: The question says a 'single still mark' is seen at 1200 and again at 2400 flashes/min, but the answer justifies the 1200 rpm reading with k = 1 and 2, and the 600 rpm reading with k = 2 and 4. With one painted mark, k = 2 shows two marks 180° apart and k = 4 shows four marks, not a single mark. So the observation as worded rules out both readings the answer gives; a single still mark at both rates would actually fit n = 2400 rpm (k = 1/2 at 1200/min, k = 1 at 2400/min) and its multiples. Question and answer contradict each other.
fix: Word the observation as 'a still image of the painted mark at 1200 flashes/min and again at 2400 flashes/min' (no 'single'). Then the answer is sound: 1200 rpm with k = 1 and 2, or 600 rpm with k = 2 and 4, so the pair alone is ambiguous. In the last sentence, replace 'sweep up from a low rate to catch the first still image' with 'lower the rate from a high value and stop at the first single still image'.

problem: 'Below the fundamental you see several marks and read a fraction' mixes up the two cases. At an exact sub-multiple of the fundamental (f = (n/60)/m) the mark looks like one single still mark and the dial reads a fraction of the true speed. It is above the fundamental, at k = 2 or 3, that you see k separate images of the one mark.
fix: Write: 'At k = 2 or 3 the image is still but you see two or three copies of the mark, and the dial reads two or three times the true speed. At a whole-number fraction of the fundamental you see one still mark again and read half, or a third, of the true speed.'

where: Section 3, frequency-to-voltage formula and Worked example 2
problem: Vout = Vref × T × fin holds only while the pulse width T is shorter than the input period, that is fin ≤ 1/T. If the input frequency rises above 1/T the pulses run into each other, the monostable output stays high, and Vout saturates at Vref instead of rising further. The text does not state this limit.
fix: Add: 'The formula holds for fin ≤ 1/T; above 1/T the output flattens at Vref, so set T for the highest frequency you expect to measure.' (In Worked example 2, T = 200 µs and fin = 250 Hz, so it is well inside the limit.)

problem: The letter p means pole pairs in the AC tachogenerator formula and number of painted marks in the stroboscope formula, two sections apart. A student revising quickly can carry the wrong meaning across.
fix: Keep p for pole pairs in Section 1 and use z for the number of marks in Section 2: f = k z n / 60, with z the number of marks painted on the shaft.
